newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices close up 3/4 point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices close up 3/4 point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended up 3/4 of a point Friday, but lagged the U.S. government market where the 30-year bond closed up 1-1/4 points.

High-grade issues improved by seven to eight basis points, while dollar bonds ended the session quoted up 3/4, a municipal analyst said. Dollar bonds opened flat, added 3/8 of a point by noon and another 3/8 point by day's end.

The government market's 30-year bond ended up 1-8/32 at 98-1/32 to yield 6.78 percent, the lowest closing yield since February 26. In debt futures, the September municipal contract was up 1-1/32 at 117-9/32. The September T-bond contract was up 1-7/32 111-7/32. The MOB spread was at 194 ticks.

On the economic front, the government offered a mixed picture of the U.S. labor market in May. It reported that the employment rate had fallen to 4.8 percent, but also reported a sharp deceleration in job growth for the month. Payrolls expanded by 138,000 jobs in May after swelling by 323,000 new jobs in April.
U.S. Treasury prices turned higher at late morning amid talk of a delay in the European Economic and Monetary Union that was said to spur foreign buying of U.S. assets.
Looking ahead to next week, some $4.8 billion of fresh debt is expected. It should be the largest weekly total so far in 1997, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
"(There are) a lot of competitive deals, so there's a lot of opportunities to make mistakes," one trader said, adding that players are uncertain about where levels are.
The competitive slate is expected to contain 89 sales totaling $2 billion. A $225 million Virginia Housing Development Authority deal on Tuesday is the largest.
